questions.q: A nibble consists of how many bits?
questions.solution: A nibble is half a byte: 4 bits. A byte is 8 bits; a word is CPU-dependent (16/32/64 bits).
questions.shortcut: Nibble = half a byte = 4 bits ('nybble nibbles off half').

questions.q: Under the IT Act, cyber terrorism is dealt with in:
questions.solution: Section 66F covers cyber terrorism - acts threatening India's sovereignty, integrity or security through computers - punishable with imprisonment that may extend to life.

questions.q: Which shortcut takes a web browser back to the previously visited page?
questions.solution: Alt+Left goes back and Alt+Right goes forward. Alt+Home opens the home page, and Ctrl+Left moves the cursor one word left in a text box.

questions.q: In MS Excel, pressing Ctrl+Space selects:
questions.solution: Ctrl+Space selects the whole column of the active cell and Shift+Space selects the whole row. Ctrl+A selects the data region, or the whole sheet if pressed again.
questions.shortcut: Ctrl and Column both start with C; Shift+Space = row.

questions.q:
Select the word which is most opposite in meaning to the given word.

PUNCTUAL
questions.solution: *Punctual* = exactly on time. Its opposite is **late**. 'Early' is not the opposite — arriving early is still not punctual in the strict sense, and SSC's key follows 'late'; 'prompt/regular' are near-synonyms.
questions.shortcut: Time-axis test: on time ↔ behind time.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the sentence: 'Please do not touch the exhibits.'
options: You are requested not to touch the exhibits.
The exhibits are requested not to be touched.
You are requested to touch not the exhibits.
You are request not to touch the exhibits.
questions.solution: A polite please-sentence takes the frame **You are requested not to + V1**: *You are requested not to touch the exhibits.* Making the exhibits the requested party garbles the frame; 'to touch not' misplaces the negative; 'are request' drops the -ed.
questions.shortcut: please + not → requested not to + V1.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** Water is the source of all life. **P:** Industries release effluents into the rivers. **Q:** Groundwater levels are falling every year. **R:** We must harvest rainwater without delay. **S:** Cities dump untreated sewage into the same rivers. **6.** Otherwise the taps of tomorrow will run dry.
questions.solution: **P** (industrial pollution) → **S** (city sewage, 'the same rivers' needs P's rivers) → **Q** (falling groundwater completes the crisis) → **R** (the remedy) before S6. PSQR.
questions.shortcut: 'The same rivers' locks S after P; remedy (must) sits last before S6.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Hardly **the results had been announced** when the servers crashed.
questions.solution: Fronted **Hardly** demands inversion: hardly **had the results been announced** when…. The original keeps statement order; 'the results had announce' breaks the participle and the order.

questions.q: The slogan **'Do or Die'** was given by Gandhi during the —
questions.solution: Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' on **8 August 1942** at **Gowalia Tank, Bombay**, when the Quit India resolution was passed.
questions.shortcut: 1942 = last big push → last-chance slogan 'Do or Die'.

questions.q: The five-kingdom classification of living organisms was proposed by:
questions.solution: **R.H. Whittaker** proposed the five kingdoms — Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia — in **1969**. Linnaeus gave binomial nomenclature and the two-kingdom system.
questions.shortcut: My Pet Fish Plays Alone — Whittaker.

questions.q: Which Delhi Sultan introduced the silver **tanka** and the copper **jital**?
questions.solution: **Iltutmish** issued the standard Arabic coins — silver tanka and copper jital — and also organised the **iqta** system and the Group of Forty.

questions.q: Hydraulic brakes in vehicles work on the principle of:
questions.solution: **Pascal's law**: pressure applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted equally in all directions. Hydraulic brakes, lifts and presses use it.

questions.q: Find the HCF of $\frac{8}{9}$, $\frac{16}{27}$ and $\frac{20}{81}$.
questions.solution:
HCF of numerators: $\gcd(8, 16, 20) = 4$. LCM of denominators: $\text{LCM}(9, 27, 81) = 81$.
HCF $= \frac{4}{81}$.

questions.q: What is the smallest six-digit number exactly divisible by 111?
How many even factors does 1080 have?
questions.solution:
$1080 = 2^3 \times 3^3 \times 5$. Total factors $= 4 \times 4 \times 2 = 32$.
Odd factors (power of 2 = 0): $4 \times 2 = 8$.
Even factors $= 32 - 8 = 24$.
questions.shortcut: Force at least one 2: exponent of 2 has 3 choices (1, 2, 3) ⇒ $3 \times 4 \times 2 = 24$.

questions.q: $19^{32} - 11^{32}$ is divisible by:
questions.solution:
$a^n - b^n$ is always divisible by $a - b = 8$.
Since $n = 32$ is even, it is also divisible by $a + b = 30$.
So it is divisible by **both 30 and 8**.
questions.shortcut: Even power difference → both (a − b) and (a + b).

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**121, 169, 225, 289**
questions.solution: All four are perfect squares: 11², 13², 15², 17² - so 'square' cannot decide. Level two: 11, 13 and 17 are **prime**; 15 = 3 × 5 is not → **225**.
questions.shortcut: All squares? Look at the roots. Also 225 is the only one ending in 5.

questions.q: In a certain code, **DIG is coded 22** — two more than the sum of the positions. How is **BIG** coded?
questions.solution: D + I + G = 4 + 9 + 7 = 20, and 20 + 2 = 22 ✓. BIG = 2 + 9 + 7 = 18, plus 2 = **20**. (18 alone forgets the step.)

questions.q: If the signs **− and × are interchanged**, what is the value of **12 − 4 × 3 + 20 ÷ 5**?
questions.solution: After the swap: **12 × 4 − 3 + 20 ÷ 5**. 12 × 4 = 48 and 20 ÷ 5 = 4. Then 48 − 3 + 4 = **49**. (4 is the unswapped value; 13 is the left-to-right value.)
questions.shortcut: Interchange is two-way: − becomes × and × becomes −.

questions.q:
**Statements:** Some rings are gold.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some rings are silver.
II. No ring is silver.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.solution: Gold is a decoy — silver is untouched, so neither conclusion is provable. Some/No on the same pair = complementary. **Either I or II follows.**
questions.shortcut: Ignore the unused statement; judge only the conclusion pair.
